correctness.rationale: The submitted source fixes all twenty graph labels and all unit edge lengths. Vertex-ball distance taxonomy proves the maximal-facet list exactly. The included standalone executable exhausts 430 and 81,233 nonempty faces at the only nontrivial radius levels, verifies 130 and 39,641 elementary simplicial free-face pairs, and reduces every residual signed integer boundary by unimodular ±1 pivots to a zero remainder. Full residual vectors (20,80,70) and (19,159,558,811,404) with exact integer ranks (19,55) and (18,141,417,389) imply respectively integral groups Z^6/Z^15 and Z^5/Z^15, without torsion. Independent mod-two boundary ranks coincide. Degree separation makes the displayed persistence maps zero; all remaining radius regimes are proved from integral graph distances and a radius-three universal ball. This is an exhaustive finite result, not a claim extrapolated to other graphs.

value.rationale: The Folkman graph is the canonical smallest 4-regular semisymmetric graph, while graph-ball nerves are motivated intrinsic topological invariants. The result fixes the complete integral vertex-ball barcode with two mixed-dimensional transitions, across four positive homological degrees, and proves torsion absence for the actual 81,233-face even-scale stage. The ranks distinguish a structured high-symmetry graph from hypercube/complete-multipartite graph Čech families and from the already-known Rips complexes; they furnish a reproducible benchmark for comparing persistent topology of regular bipartite graphs whose vertex orbits differ. The exact finite classification resolves a natural invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a routine paraphrase of a previous result; no full graph-geometric Čech or homotopy classification is asserted.
